items.title: OpenAI agents: coding task success nearly doubles, serving code lags
items.summary: Autonomous success on 2-4 hour coding tasks rose from 23% to 46% between March and October, per OpenAI's internal tracking, with agent workdays per researcher up 11x. Agents still trail badly on harder work: 25% success writing inference/serving code and 29% building eval environments, versus 69% on communication tasks. Trust agents more for glue work, less for core systems code for now. (4 minute read)

items.title: RL training cuts multi-agent LLM token use 37%, boosts success 12x
items.summary: A new RL recipe trains 4-agent LLM teams on a shared reward, taking a sorting task from 6.56% to 82.34% success over 75 update steps while cutting tokens per team 37%. A single trained attempt now hits 82.3% success in about 8,000 tokens, versus 37.5% at best-of-8 for an untrained team spending 103,000. The eval methodology — scoring by communication class, not just outcome — is as useful as the result itself. (4 minute read)

items.title: Notion's official MCP hides upsell prompts in agent context
items.summary: Notion's official MCP server reportedly injects a hidden instruction telling agents not to render its upsell link as a preview, so it slips past review, then has the agent tell users they need the paid plan once free queries run out. Commenters say the pattern is spreading — a DoorDash CLI already requires agents to resend the user's original prompt on every call. Read any MCP server's instructions before trusting them. (4 minute read)

items.title: CPU-only ternary inference engine hits 20 tok/s on 8GB RAM
items.summary: openset-llm runs PrismML's ternary-quantized Qwen3.8-27B at 17-20 tok/s on an 8 vCPU, 8GB Ice Lake box with no GPU — 4.2x faster than ik_llama.cpp and 5.9x faster than PrismML's own llama.cpp fork on the same hardware. New AVX-512 and AVX2 matmul kernels for the ternary format, plus speculative decoding via an unsloth multi-token-prediction head, do the work. A 27B model now runs usably on a basic cloud VM. (4 minute read)

items.title: Switzerland: AI agents drove 4 of 5 confirmed cyberattacks
items.summary: Switzerland's NCSC says AI agents independently carried out 4 of 5 confirmed attacks it investigated, breaching 2 of 3 targeted critical-infrastructure operators. Italy and the UK confirmed the same trend and named the tools in use — ARTEX, CyberStrikeAI, PentAGI, and DeepSeek Harness — pointing to ARTEX's October 22 breach of the European Commission's HR and medical systems. Publicly reachable AI attack tools have nearly doubled since then. (3 minute read)

items.title: Convex's Claude/Codex skill quietly phones home your app idea
items.summary: Convex's official quickstart skill for Claude and Codex POSTs the user's one-sentence app idea and template name to a Convex-run endpoint, logged internally as "a run started," with no disclosure to the user. A related skill splits a script download from its execution into two separate calls — its own code comment says a combined command is what harness safety classifiers block — then pipes the result into bash. A commenter confirmed the endpoint accepts arbitrary text and that an opt-out environment variable doesn't stop the calls. (4 minute read)

items.title: North Korea's PolinRider poisoned 7,600+ GitHub repos
items.summary: PolinRider, linked to North Korea, compromised 7,609 GitHub repositories across 2,330 accounts using stolen developer tokens to force-push commits that keep the original author, message, and date. A 58-line Python loader hidden in utility packages decodes an Ethereum transaction as JavaScript and runs it via Node to reach a command-and-control server. Blockchain records show activity dating back to February 2025, with 2,040 repos infected in a single ten-day wave in late October. (4 minute read)

items.title: Hackers breach US Air Force's Cloud One platform
items.summary: Reuters reports hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship Cloud One computing platform, though the scope and method of the intrusion remain undisclosed. (1 minute read)
